newsitem.title: USA: Florida launches sterile Medfly assault.
newsitem.headline: Florida launches sterile Medfly assault.

text.p: Millions of sterile Mediterranean fruit flies were released over Tampa Friday in a new effort to eradicate the feared agricultural pest, plague of Florida's $8-billion citrus industry.
The use of sterile flies is a form of biological warfare. State officials say the sterile flies will mate with medflies in the wild and die after mating, thereby ending the reproductive cycle.
Release of the flies came after nearly two months of controversial aerial spraying of the pesticide malathion in the region of Florida's west coast where the pesky fruit flies were discovered May 28.

Authorities have sprayed hundreds of acres in Hillsborough and Polk counties, among the most productive citrus regions in Florida. Many residents oppose malathion spraying because they fear it will contaminate their water supplies.
"We've been anxious to get to this stage," Florida Agriculture Commission Bob Crawford said before the first flight carrying sterile flies took off.
"We know the people in this area are wanting to eliminate the aerial spraying as soon as possible, and that is what we are doing."

Crawford said malathion spraying would continue in certain areas for a few more weeks. A one-square-mile area in nearby Orange county near Orlando was scheduled to be sprayed Sunday because four medflies were found there recently.
The flies are being brought from Guatemala and are treated with radiation to make them sterile. Several hundred million will be released each week until the wild medflies are eradicated.
Mediterranean fruit flies are considered one of the most dangerous agricultural pests. They attack and destroy more than 200 varieties of fruits and vegetables.
